subject: Request: temporary no-PO onboarding / grace-window for MerchantIO trial
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@merchantio.com
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding / trial billing question - MerchantIO

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — MerchantIO is excited to kick off the 30-day pilot. Our legal can sign the MSA quickly; the only snag on our side is that our accounting team issues vendor invoices and prefers to start the first month without a Purchase Order while we finalize their ERP onboarding.

Can Redwood accommodate a short, conditional no-PO grace window for the first invoice (30 days) so we can start the integration immediately? We can provide W-9 and a bank verification letter now, and commit to normal PO process from month two onward.

If there are special invoicing codes or a cap you require during the trial, let us know — we want to move fast but stay within your controls.

Attached: merchantio_vendor_form.pdf (vendor intake form)

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Finance Operations
MerchantIO

[Attachment: merchantio_vendor_form.pdf (application/pdf) referenced]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantio.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding / trial billing question - MerchantIO

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for sending the intake form.

Short answer: we do have a path for a limited no-PO "grace window" for pilots, but procurement requires a few items before we can sign off. Vanessa / Naomi from Procurement & Finance are cc'd — can you confirm you can provide:

- Completed vendor intake (you already attached)
- W-9 or equivalent tax form (PDF)
- Bank verification or vendor-bank letter (scanned)
- Invoice cap for the pilot (suggested: $5,000)
- Point of contact for month-two PO setup (name/email)

If Procurement signs off, we'll route the first invoice through a temporary billing code and tag it as "pilot - conditional no-PO" so Finance can track it. Vanessa — any extra controls or time limits we should attach?

Marcus
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Inline: quick link to HubSpot opportunity: https://hubspot.company/opps/merchantio-8731]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@merchantio.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding / trial billing question - MerchantIO

Hi all — I reviewed MerchantIO's intake and this is what Procurement needs to approve a temporary no-PO trial: 

1) Evidence: W-9 + bank verification (accepted formats: PDF, letterhead scan).
2) Administrative guardrails (Procurement will issue conditional approval subject to):
   - Pilot window: up to 45 days from first invoice date.
   - Dollar cap: $6,000 total for the trial (we can accept Elena's $5k suggestion; I'll set $6k to give buffer).
   - Invoice routing: vendor must send invoices to payments@redwood.com with subject line: "MerchantIO - PILOT INVOICE - noPO".
   - PO commit: vendor must designate a named contact to complete PO setup by day 30 of the pilot (we'll push for PO to be in place by invoice #2).
3) Approvals: Naomi (Finance) must confirm the special billing code (PROC-PILOT-21) will allow automated tagging for GL/expense tracking.

If Elena can attach W-9 and bank letter, Procurement can approve the conditional no-PO path today and escalate to Finance for final code confirmation. If anything else pops up (SLA, data residency), we can add conditions, but this is the standard minimal set.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

[Action items]
- Elena: attach W-9 and bank verification (by EOD Wed)
- MerchantIO: confirm pilot cap ($6,000) and PO lead
- Naomi: confirm billing code and any GL notes
